balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities attributable to ordinary shareholders; total equity (incl. hybrid & NCI) adds SSE's perpetual hybrid capital instruments and non-controlling interests; both are plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For SSE plc: the gap between the two equity lines widened sharply in FY2026 on the ~£2bn November 2025 placing plus hybrid issuance -- equity that grows through capital raises or revaluations is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • The hybrid/NCI share of total equity, since hybrid coupons rank ahead of ordinary dividends

beforeExceptionals.title: Operating and attributable profit before exceptional items
beforeExceptionals.content:
SSE reports an adjusted operating profit and adjusted attributable profit alongside its statutory IFRS figures, stripping out exceptional items and, crucially, the mark-to-market movements on commodity and FX derivatives that do not settle in cash.

For SSE plc: the statutory Operating Income / Net Income chart above is not a reliable earnings trend on its own -- FY2023 statutory operating income was -£146.3m, on a year SSE itself called a record, purely from derivative re-measurement. The financial-parser and DCF analysis both anchor on these before-exceptional lines instead.

What to watch:

  • Whether the before-exceptional trend is actually growing, independent of the statutory swings
  • The size of the adjustment each year (statutory vs. before-exceptional) -- a growing gap deserves scrutiny of what is being excluded

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For SSE plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For SSE plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For SSE plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For SSE plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For SSE plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For SSE plc: these are the statutory IFRS lines, and SSE's operating income and net income swing heavily on mark-to-market derivative re-measurements that have nothing to do with the underlying business -- FY2023 statutory operating income was -£146.3m despite SSE calling it a record year. See the "Operating Profit & Attributable Profit (before exceptionals)" chart below for the adjusted trend SSE and this analysis actually anchor on.

What to watch:

  • The gap between this statutory chart and the before-exceptionals chart below
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For SSE plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For SSE plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
